newsitem.title: PANAMA: Panama eyes APEC with Philippines' Ramos' visit.
newsitem.headline: Panama eyes APEC with Philippines' Ramos' visit.

text.p: Panama is keen to broaden ties with countries in the Asia-Pacific and will use a visit next week by Philippine President Fidel Ramos to boost trade with the region, a government official said Wednesday.
"Panama is interested in being included in APEC because it is a gateway to the Pacific," a Commerce Ministry spokesman said.
The Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum, APEC, groups 18 nations, representing the Asian Pacific Rim plus Canada, Chile, Mexico and the United States.
Ramos will be in Panama May 13-15. He will be accompanied by a 200-person delegation and is due to meet privately with President Ernesto Perez Balladares and sign various accords.

"The idea is for Panama to participate in all associations that gives growth opportunities and boosts commerce. There is already Asian investment in ports, the canal and the Colon free-trade zone and interest is increasing," he said.
Ramos will also discuss investment opportunities in U.S. military installations that are scheduled to be turned over to Panamanian control in 1999.
